meta.description: Detects allele-specific transcription factor or histone modification binding from heterozygous-variant ChIP-seq using WASP, RASQUAL, BaalChIP with measured RAF or gDNA correction, and an explicitly external-only AlleleSeq route.

scientific_integrity.detail: No output fabricated study identifiers, sample sizes, p-values, efficacy data, or live execution. Public and synthetic fixtures are labeled, and inaccessible BaalChIP and AlleleSeq model execution was not credited.

practice_boundaries.detail: The skill remains a research-analysis workflow, makes no patient-specific diagnosis or treatment recommendation, and keeps prediction, within-sample ASB, and population QTL interpretations distinct.

methodological_ground.detail: Mapping bias, imprinting, chrX, allele dose, replicate depth, convergence, and multiplicity are handled explicitly. The open BaalChIP release-label defect is a reproducibility binding error, not a statistical-method fallacy.

code_usability.detail: All accessible code parsed and executed: R contracts, Python tests, RAF and gDNA preflights, paired WASP, WASP HDF5, and a two-feature public RASQUAL cohort. BaalChIP full-model and AlleleSeq full-toolchain execution remain explicitly unavailable and were not scored as successes.

functional_suitability.note: The four advertised routes, confounders, outputs, and scientific boundaries are covered. The BaalChIP 1.38.0 release is incorrectly bound to Bioconductor 3.22 rather than 3.23, so that route is not reproducible from the stated installation contract.

reliability.note: Accessible runners fail closed, preserve atomicity, reject output reuse, and expose structured errors. Full BaalChIP terminal branches remain unexecuted, and the release mismatch obstructs a clean environment rebuild.

performance_context.note: Progressive disclosure and bounded runners are efficient; the legacy and Bioconductor surfaces necessarily carry substantial dependency cost.

agent_usability.note: Routing, preflights, stop conditions, output contracts, and interpretation guidance are clear. One incompatible BaalChIP release label can send an agent to the wrong package universe.

human_usability.note: Natural triggers, method selection, prerequisite lists, and troubleshooting boundaries make the skill discoverable without weakening scientific input validation.

security.note: No credentials, raw-code evaluation, shell interpolation of user commands, broad deletion, or private-data retention appears; paths and schemas are validated before execution.

maintainability.note: Documentation, contracts, model runner, cohort driver, and focused tests are cleanly separated. A live BaalChIP integration test is still blocked by the unresolved environment binding.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision, progressive disclosure, composable file contracts, idempotent output refusal, and explicit external routing are strong; source identity for the AlleleSeq checkout is not bound to the linked repository.

inputs.label: Paired-end WASP mapping-bias route
inputs.note: Fresh v0.3.4 paired execution and provider HDF5 construction passed exact filenames, shapes, pairing, and stage-count invariants.

assertions.note: Fresh output names were input.remap.fq1.gz and input.remap.fq2.gz, and both contained six records.

assertions.text: Every final WASP alignment remains paired.
assertions.note: All four final alignments carried the paired flag.

assertions.text: Final alignments equal direct keeps plus remap keeps and do not exceed input alignments.
assertions.note: The fresh run satisfied final=4, direct+remap=4, and input=4.

assertions.text: The provider chromosome-22 IMPUTE2 and haplotype inputs produce the expected HDF5 shapes.
assertions.note: All four expected /chr22 shapes were independently inspected and matched.

assertions.text: The workflow reports observed attrition rather than assuming a fixed percentage.
assertions.note: The documentation requires input, remap, retained, tested, and significant counts.

assertions.note: C11orf21 and TSPAN32 each appeared once in the two-row result family.

assertions.text: Every emitted row satisfies the 25-column RASQUAL contract with finite phi and convergence zero.
assertions.note: Both public rows passed all three checks.

assertions.text: The wrapper derives finite raw p-values and Benjamini-Hochberg q-values across the emitted cohort family.
assertions.note: Both appended p and cohort q fields were finite and within [0,1].

key_strengths: The paired WASP route now matches the pinned provider filenames and preserves explicit fragment-count and pairing invariants.
The RASQUAL driver performs validated binary preparation, exact feature iteration, strict output parsing, convergence checks, and family-level BH correction.
The BaalChIP runner validates scientific inputs before package loading, records the actual correction source, refuses overwrite, and cleans owned staging on failure.
Imprinting, chrX, copy number, mapping bias, low depth, and prediction-versus-measurement boundaries are scientifically explicit.
Unavailable BaalChIP and AlleleSeq components are classified honestly rather than receiving execution credit.

recommendations.title: CBA-009: Correct the BaalChIP release binding
recommendations.problem: The candidate states that BaalChIP 1.38.0 is a Bioconductor 3.22 contract, but the exact staged package identifies itself as RELEASE_3_23 and Repository Bioconductor 3.23. The prepared R library is BiocVersion 3.22.0, so the documented installation command cannot reproduce the runner's enforced version in the stated environment.
recommendations.root_cause: The tested source version was updated without updating the release label and base R/Bioconductor compatibility contract.
recommendations.fix: Choose one coherent binding: either move the documented and tested environment to Bioconductor 3.23 with its compatible R release, or pin the runner and documentation to the actual BaalChIP version supplied by Bioconductor 3.22. Rebuild the bounded environment and rerun the package-load, full-model, no-variant, and no-call paths.

recommendations.title: CBA-010: Bind AlleleSeq to the tested repository
recommendations.problem: The claim-level source table links gersteinlab/AlleleSeq while the exact prepared checkout for commit cfe8acf is trgaleev/AlleleSeq2.
recommendations.root_cause: The method's canonical project link and the concrete implementation checkout were treated as the same source identity.
recommendations.fix: Name and link the exact implementation repository used for cfe8acf, while retaining the paper and canonical project separately if both are scientifically useful.
